inventory.visualPurpose: The autonomic/somatic wiring figure (book 234): the two-neuron chains, their transmitters, and every receptor chip
inventory.sourceFigureDescription: VECTOR LINE ART, no raster (pdfimages: zero raster images; VLM attempted twice on scripts/usmle-pipeline/ph9-vlm-census.ts and failed 401 missing X-Token both times — labels read via the pdftotext text layer): ONE large wiring figure — AUTONOMIC split into a Parasympathetic column (Brainstem origin; Preganglionic neuron (long) → Nn ganglion near the target → Postganglionic neuron (short) → ACh → M₁, M₂, M₃ on Smooth muscle, gland cells, nerve terminals, cardiac muscle) and a Sympathetic column (Spinal cord origin; Preganglionic neuron (short) → Nn in the Sympathetic chain → Postganglionic neuron (long) → NE → α1, α2, β1, β2 on the same target set and Cardiac muscle, vessels, plus α1, α2, β1, D1 on Renal vasculature smooth muscle), beside a SOMATIC column (Voluntary motor nerve → ACh → Neuromuscular junction with Nm on Skeletal muscle). The sympathetic exceptions print on the same figure: the Adrenal gland (medulla) with its own Nn, DIRECTLY innervated by a preganglionic sympathetic fiber and releasing Epi + NE into Blood (catecholamine transmission); and the Sweat glands — part of the sympathetic pathway but innervated by cholinergic fibers (ACh → M₃; sympathetic nervous system results in a “chold” sweat, the source's own typo) — with a standalone “D” label printing beneath “Sweat glands” in the text layer. Three rule lines print under the figure: the parasympathetic nerve list (pelvic splanchnic nerves and CNs III, VII, IX, and X), the direct adrenal-medulla line, and the sweat-gland cholinergic exception.
